soilKey 0.9.253 (2026-10-13)

SiBCS key: the histic horizon with the whole of its thickness, and the thickness the key asks of it

The horizonte hístico (SiBCS 2018, Cap. 2, p. 49-50) results from plant residues laid down at the surface, “ainda que, no presente, possa encontrar-se recoberto por horizontes ou depósitos minerais”, and has to be 20 cm thick or more, or 10 cm or more over a lithic contact. The Organossolos (Cap. 4, p. 111) have a horizonte hístico of “20 cm ou mais, quando sobrejacente a um contato lítico”, or of “40 cm ou mais, contínuo ou cumulativo nos primeiros 80 cm a partir da superfície do solo”.

Two things in the code were not that:

  • Only a layer that starts within 5 cm of the surface was looked at. A horizon described in sub-horizons counted the first of them alone (BDsolos ES 8651: Oo1 0-15, Oo2 15-32, Oo3 32-80 cm, with 39 to 45% of organic carbon, keyed Neossolos by the 15 cm of its Oo1), and a buried horizon was not seen (SE 6560: 2Hdz from 22 cm down).
  • Any horizonte hístico made an Organossolo. One of 20 to 39 cm over a mineral horizon did, although the key asks 40 cm of it and places those soils further down (Gleissolos Melânicos, Cambissolos Hísticos).

Now:

  • horizonte_histico() takes the organic layers wherever they lie; adjoining ones make one horizon, with the thickness of all of them; a horizon passes with 20 cm, or with 10 cm when the layer right below it is an R or a Cr. What makes a layer organic is as before. The evidence lists each run of adjoining organic layers with its limits and its thickness.
  • The Organossolos step asks (a) 20 cm or more of a horizon that lies on a lithic contact, or (b) 40 cm or more of horizonte hístico within the first 80 cm, in one section or added up.
  • Not tested, as before: the volume of plant tissue is no column of the profile, so the greater thickness asked where it makes 75% or more of the horizon (40 cm in the horizon, 60 cm in the key) is not asked. The earlier code read it from the column of worm holes, which is not that, in a test that could not change the result.

soilKey 0.9.252 (2026-10-13)

SiBCS key: item (c) of the Neossolos step by its letter

The Neossolos are soils with no diagnostic B that satisfy, among others (SiBCS 2018, Cap. 4, p. 112), “c) Ausência de horizonte vértico imediatamente abaixo de horizonte A”. The step tested a vertic horizon that begins within 50 cm, whatever lay between it and the A.

Decided on 2026-10-13: by the letter.

  • The first layer of the vertic horizon has to be right below an A. The horizons of transition from the A (AB, AC) count with the A, as they do in the thickness of the A chernozêmico (p. 51).
  • A vertic horizon that begins at the surface is there too.
  • A profile with no horizon designation is tested as before.

soilKey 0.9.251 (2026-10-13)

BDsolos: the cerosidade written in the text of the horizon is read

The export has the cerosidade in two structured columns, its amount and its grade, and also as the survey wrote it, in the text of the horizon (“Descrição Original”). The key asks for both: the B textural by its cerosidade (SiBCS 2018, Cap. 2, p. 56, item i), the B nítico “em quantidade no mínimo comum e com grau forte ou moderado” (p. 62), the B latossólico “no máximo pouca e fraca” (p. 59). In 142 horizons the text names the cerosidade and the two columns are empty.

load_bdsolos_csv() reads the amount and the grade from the text, each where its own cell is empty, by the rule decided on 2026-10-13 for the slickensides: what is written beside the term.

  • The words right after “cerosidade” are read as long as they are amounts, grades or words that join them (“cerosidade comum e moderada”, “cerosidade fraca e pouca”), or the one word right before it (“pouca cerosidade”). Two grades or two amounts are a range (“fraca a moderada”).
  • Nothing is read from a bare mention (“presença de cerosidade”), a denial (“sem cerosidade”), or words that are of something else (“cor da cerosidade (10YR 4/4) com mosqueado pouco”, “comum e moderada muito firme”).
  • The spellings of the export are read (“serosidade”, “crosidade”).

The reader was checked against the structured columns, in the horizons that have both: the amount is the same in 2,150 of 2,190 (98.2%) and the grade in 2,172 of 2,208 (98.4%). Where they differ the text and the cell say different things (“comum e fraca” beside a cell “Pouca”); the cell is kept. In the horizons with empty cells every phrase was read: the loader fills the amount in 123 layers and the grade in 123, 127 layers of 111 profiles in all.

soilKey 0.9.250 (2026-10-13)

SiBCS key: in a profile of the older notation the A2 is the E and the B3 is the BC

The notation in use in Brazil until 1988 named the eluvial horizon “A2” and the horizon of transition from the B to the C “B3”; the present notation writes them “E” and “BC”. The book asks about both by their present names: an E above the B makes a B textural (SiBCS 2018, Cap. 2, p. 55, item f), and the BC is left out of the B in the textural ratio (p. 56, note 4). The key read the A2 as an A and the B3 as a B.

Decided on 2026-10-13: both are read by what they name.

  • A profile is taken to be in the older notation when one of its horizons is a B followed at once by a number (“B1”, “B21t”, “IIB3”) or a “(B)”. In the present notation the number comes after the letters (“Bt1”), and “A1, A2” beside “Bt1, Bt2” stay two parts of an A. Of the 7,593 profiles of the national BDsolos export with a reference order, 3,167 are in the older notation; 250 of them have an A2 and 853 a B3.
  • In such a profile “A2”, “A21” and “B3t” are read “E”, “E1” and “BCt”, by every test of the SiBCS key that reads a designation. The horizon data keep the designation as written, and WRB and USDA are not changed.

That the A2 is the eluvial horizon and the B3 the transition to the C is the notation as I know it from the surveys; SiBCS 2018 does not state the correspondence, and it is for confirmation.

soilKey 0.9.249 (2026-10-13)

SiBCS key: the horizons the B latossólico does not present take out their own layers

The book (SiBCS 2018, Cap. 2, p. 59): “o horizonte B latossólico é um horizonte subsuperficial que não apresenta características diagnósticas de horizontes glei, B textural, B nítico e plíntico”. The sentence is about the horizon. B_latossolico() voided the B latossólico of the whole profile when one of three things was found in any layer: the gleyic properties of WRB (mottles of 5% or more in a layer that begins within 50 cm), the plinthic horizon of WRB, or a B nítico.

Decided on 2026-10-13: those horizons take out their own layers only.

  • The layers of a horizonte glei, of a horizonte plíntico and of a B nítico, as SiBCS defines them, are no part of the B latossólico, with those of the B textural, which were already left out. The layers that are left make the horizon if they make its 50 cm.
  • Mottles alone make no horizonte glei, so that a red B with common mottles keeps its B latossólico.
  • latossolo() applies to the B nítico the rule it applied to the B textural (Cap. 4, p. 110): a B latossólico below a B nítico makes no Latossolo.

soilKey 0.9.248 (2026-10-13)

SiBCS key: the “p1” of B and C horizons is the “pl” of plinthite

The surveys before the present notation wrote plinthite “pl” (B21pl, Cpl), which the morphological mode reads as the horizonte plíntico since 0.9.234. The BDsolos export has it also as “p1”, the letter “l” written as the figure 1: B2tp1, B22tp1, Cp1, B2tp1cn, in 219 horizons of 145 profiles. Of those profiles, 135 have “plíntico”, “laterita” or “concrecionário” in their reference name, and 95 have a reference in Plintossolos.

horizonte_plintico() reads the “p1” of a B or C horizon as “pl”, in the morphological mode only, with the same 15 cm. It is not read where the profile numbers such horizons on (“Bp1” beside “Bp2”): no B or C of the export is written with “p2”, so that the “p1” there is not the first of a series. “Ap1” is a ploughed layer and stays one.

soilKey 0.9.247 (2026-10-13)

SiBCS key: the “ir” of the older surveys is a B espódico in the morphological mode

The surveys that predate the present horizon notation write the illuvial iron of a B horizon “ir” (Bir, B2ir, B22irx), where the present notation writes “s”. The morphological mode, which reads the diagnostic horizon from the designation where the analyses do not show it, read “h” and “s” as the B espódico. A B with “ir” and no “h” was not read.

B_espodico() reads it now, in that mode only. In the national BDsolos export 26 profiles carry “ir” in a horizon designation, and all 26 have a reference in Espodossolos. In the morphological mode 19 of them keyed there already and 25 do now; the other one, with 16.5% of organic carbon in an A of 40 cm, keys Organossolos (AM 10502).

The reading is that of SiBCS only: spodic(), which serves WRB and USDA, is not changed.

soilKey 0.9.246 (2026-10-13)

SiBCS key: the minimum thickness of a horizon is that of its adjoining sub-horizons

The book states each minimum of the horizon: the B incipiente “deve ter no mínimo 10 cm de espessura” (SiBCS 2018, Cap. 2, p. 60), the B nítico “Espessura de 30 cm ou mais” (p. 62), the horizonte glei “com espessura de 15 cm ou mais” (p. 69), the concrecionário “no mínimo 30 cm de espessura” (p. 68), the sulfúrico “15 cm ou mais de espessura” (p. 72). Each was asked of one layer of the description, so that a horizon described in two sub-horizons thinner than the minimum did not pass, whatever the two made together. The B latossólico is read by its adjoining sub-horizons since 0.9.241 and the vertic horizon since 0.9.245; the five above are now read the same way.

The horizonte sulfúrico is read so on its two paths: with jarosite, and with sulfidic material, which is tested by the WRB thionic(). That function takes a new argument, adjoining, FALSE by default: the WRB thionic horizon is tested as before.

The horizons that reach SiBCS through a WRB function (plíntico, espódico, cálcico) are not changed.

A correction to 0.9.244

mudanca_textural_abrupta() and B_planico() took a BC for the first B sub-horizon when it came before any other B. The note of 0.9.244 says that the BC is left out of the B, as in item (h) of the B textural; the code did not leave it out, and now does. Of the national export, 7 profiles have a BC as their first B; none had an abrupt change or a B plânico by it, and no figure of 0.9.244 changes.

soilKey 0.9.245 (2026-10-13)

SiBCS key: the vertic horizon by the features of the book, read also from the text of the description

Of the 72 profiles of the national BDsolos export with a reference in Vertissolos, 10 keyed there in the default mode. The book (SiBCS 2018, Cap. 2, p. 73) knows the vertic horizon by “superfícies de fricção (slickensides) em quantidade no mínimo comum, e/ou unidades estruturais cuneiformes e/ou paralelepipédicas”, asks of it “uma espessura mínima de 20 cm”, and gives it “precedência diagnóstica sobre os horizontes B incipiente, B nítico e glei”. horizonte_vertico() was the WRB horizon with other limits: slickensides only, and 20 cm of one layer. And the surveys older than the structured field sheet wrote the slickensides and the structure in the text of the horizon, which the loader did not read.

  • The loader reads the text of the horizon description. The column “Descrição Original” of the export is read for two things, where the structured columns are empty, and is not kept. The amount of slickensides is the one written beside the term (“‘’slickenside’’ comum e moderado”, “abundantes superfícies de fricção”); a mention with no amount fills nothing, as decided on 2026-10-13, and neither does an amount that belongs to another feature (“cerosidade forte e abundante apresentando slickensides”) or a comparison (“mais abundantes que o horizonte superior”). A wedge-shaped or parallelepipedic structure is added to the structure of the horizon; a structure “com tendência a paralelepipédica” is not one. The terms are read in the spellings the export has (“slikenside”, “silkensides”, “paralelepédica”). The reader was checked against every phrase of the export that holds the terms: 127 different ones for the slickensides, 36 for the structure. It reads an amount in 212 layers and the structure in 41.
  • The vertic horizon. A layer with 300 g/kg of clay or more is vertic by slickensides in amount of common or more, or by wedge-shaped or parallelepipedic structural units, with cracks of 1 cm where their width is recorded; the 20 cm are those of adjoining layers.
  • Its precedence. B_incipiente() left out the layers of the WRB vertic horizon; it leaves out those of this one.
  • The Vertissolos step (Cap. 4, p. 112) asks what its first words ask, a “relação textural insuficiente para identificar um B textural”: a profile whose B textural is identified by the textural ratio of item (h) is no Vertissolo. One identified by its cerosidade alone, with a ratio known to be below the limit, is not kept out. Where the ratio cannot be computed, the B textural keeps the profile out.
  • Item (a) of the step, “Teor de argila, após mistura e homogeneização do material de solo, nos 20 cm superficiais, de no mínimo 300 g kg-1”, is the clay of each layer weighted by what it has within the upper 20 cm. The plain mean of the layers that begin at 20 cm or above was tested.

soilKey 0.9.244 (2026-10-13)

SiBCS key: the mudança textural abrupta and the B plânico as the book states them

mudanca_textural_abrupta() was the WRB abrupt textural difference under another name: every pair of adjoining layers was compared, in the order of the rows, and no distance was asked. A jump of clay between two B horizons, or from a B to a C, was an abrupt change, and B_planico() took any layer with such a jump for the B plânico.

The book (SiBCS 2018, Cap. 1, p. 30-31): the mudança textural abrupta is “um considerável aumento no teor de argila em pequena distância na zona de transição entre o horizonte A ou E e o horizonte subjacente B”, twice the clay when the A or E has less than 200 g/kg and 200 g/kg more otherwise, “em uma distância vertical ≤ 7,5 cm”. And the B plânico (Cap. 2, p. 65) is “um tipo especial de horizonte B textural […] subjacente a horizontes A ou E, apresentando mudança textural abrupta ou transição abrupta associada à relação textural com valor dentro do especificado para o horizonte B textural (subitem h), porém calculado entre o primeiro sub-horizonte B e o horizonte imediatamente acima (A ou E)”.

  • Mudança textural abrupta. The first B horizon is compared with the horizon immediately above it, which has to be an A or an E. The distance is read from the distinctness of the transition, which the BDsolos loader brings since 0.9.241: abrupt or clear is within 7.5 cm, gradual or diffuse is not; where it is not recorded the two horizons are compared. The subgroups that ask for the attribute (“abrúpticos”) read it the same way.
  • B plânico. It is looked for in the first B sub-horizon, by one of the two ways of the book: the mudança textural abrupta, or a transition recorded as abrupt with the clay of that sub-horizon over the clay of the horizon above beyond the limit of item (h) (1.50, 1.70 or 1.80). The second way was not tested.
  • Its texture. As a type of B textural, that sub-horizon has a texture francoarenosa or finer (p. 54). The WRB property asked 15% of clay of the lower layer; the attribute of the book asks none, and without the texture the sandy Bh of 9 reference Espodossolos, 2 to 7% of clay below an E with 0 to 3%, was a B plânico in the default mode.
  • Where the colour and the structure are asked. In that first sub-horizon, as decided on 2026-10-13. Measured before the texture was asked: of any B sub-horizon, 216 profiles keyed Planossolos with 122 of that reference; of the first, 178 with 109.
  • Item (g) of the B textural reads the transition by the same function.

The first B sub-horizon is the first horizon whose designation begins with B, a BA or the B1 of the old notation included, as in item (h), which leaves out of the B only the BC. The other reading, with those as the horizon above, was measured: the B plânico changes in 20 profiles, 6 reference Planossolos lose it and 1 gains it.

A profile with no horizon designation at all is tested as before. The WRB abrupt_textural_difference() is not changed.

morphological mode 4,817 (63.4%) 4,828 (63.6%)

soilKey 0.9.243 (2026-10-13)

SiBCS key: the B latossólico is asked for its Ki

The book (SiBCS 2018, Cap. 2, p. 59, item e) asks of the B latossólico a “Relação molecular SiO2/Al2O3 (Ki) igual ou inferior a 2,2, sendo normalmente menor que 2,0”, and tells the B incipiente from it by a Ki “maior que 2,2” (p. 61). The item was not tested. The profile schema has the silica and the alumina of the sulfuric attack, from which compute_ki() gives the index, but the BDsolos loader did not read them, although the export records them in 71% of its rows.

  • load_bdsolos_csv() reads “Ataque sulfúrico - SiO2” and “- Al2O3” into sio2_sulfuric_pct and al2o3_sulfuric_pct, converted from g/kg to %. The index computed from them reproduces the Ki column of the export (99.1% of the rows of one state within 0.05).
  • In B_latossolico() a layer whose Ki is recorded above 2.20 is no B latossólico. The horizon is what is left: the adjoining sub-horizons that meet every requirement still have to make 50 cm. Where the sulfuric attack is not recorded the horizon is tested as before.

The limit is read as written and by sub-horizon, as decided on 2026-10-13 after the alternatives were measured (the limit at one decimal, so that 2.24 counts as 2.2, cost 16 profiles where this costs 23).

soilKey 0.9.242 (2026-10-13)

BDsolos: the loader reads the kind of sampling point, and the benchmark reports by it

The export marks each record, in its column “Tipo”, as “Perfil completo”, “Perfil parcial” or “Amostra extra”. The loader did not read the column. Of the 7,593 records of the national export with a reference order, 4,674 are complete profiles, 332 partial profiles and 2,587 extra samples. An extra sample is, in most cases, two sampled layers of a point (a topsoil and a subsoil sample, often with a gap between them): the thickness recorded is that of the samples, and a horizon that is asked for 50 cm cannot be shown by it. One figure for the three mixed what the key does on a described profile with what it can do on two samples.

  • load_bdsolos_csv() puts the column in site$sampling_type, as written (the double space of “Perfil parcial” made one).
  • benchmark_bdsolos() gains sampling_type = "Perfil completo": the figures of each system (accuracy, n_compared, n_correct, confusion, per_class) are those of the complete profiles, and the new by_sampling_type gives the counts of every kind and of all the records together. sampling_type = NULL counts every record, as the function did. Pedons that carry no site$sampling_type (another source, a hand-made list, a file with no “Tipo” column) are all counted, as before.
  • The BDsolos row of run_all_benchmarks() and of benchmark_unified() is drawn from complete profiles: extra samples and partial profiles are left out before the cap.

The key is not changed. On the national export, at this version:

soilKey 0.9.241 (2026-10-13)

SiBCS key: the B textural and the B latossólico are tested by the items of the book

Three things in the two horizons that separate most of the profiles of Brazil were not the book’s (SiBCS 2018, Cap. 2, p. 54-59), and one in the Neossolos step followed from them.

  • B_textural() was the WRB argic horizon: a layer with 6 percentage points of clay, a ratio of 1.4 or 20 points more than the least clayey layer anywhere above it. Item (h) of the book, the relação textural, had been joined to it; items (f), (g) and (i) were not tested.
  • B_latossolico() asked its 50 cm of each layer on its own: a B latossólico described as B1, B21 and B22 of 35 cm each was none.
  • Since 0.9.61 a B textural did not exclude the B latossólico unless its clay films were common or more, on a rule the comments attributed to Cap. 18 of the book, which deals with families and series. The book (p. 59): the B latossólico “não apresenta características diagnósticas de horizontes glei, B textural, B nítico e plíntico”. The first defect hid this one: with the thickness alone corrected, 168 reference Argissolos of the national BDsolos export became Latossolos.
  • neossolo() set a diagnostic B aside when the profile had caráter flúvico (0.9.10), because the clay increase of the argic horizon fired between the stratified C layers of the canonical Fluvisol.

The B textural

A profile with horizon designations is tested by the items of p. 55-56: a B horizon (BC excluded) of texture francoarenosa or finer and 7.5 cm or more, with one or more of

  • (f) an E horizon above it, the B having more clay and being no B espódico, plíntico or plânico;
  • (g) a mudança textural abrupta from the A or E to the B (Cap. 1, p. 30-31): twice the clay when the A or E has less than 200 g/kg, 200 g/kg more otherwise, “em uma distância vertical ≤ 7,5 cm”. The distance is read from the distinctness of the transition, which the BDsolos loader now brings (boundary_distinctness: “Abrupta” and “Clara” are within 7.5 cm, “Gradual” and “Difusa” are not); where it is not recorded the two layers are compared;
  • (h) the relação textural above 1.50, 1.70 or 1.80 according to the clay of the A. Footnote 4 asks for the “média aritmética do teor de argila total do horizonte B (excluído o BC)”; the means were weighted by the thickness. The designations are read with their material number and the old “(B)”;
  • (i) where the increase is below item (h), the cerosidade of a sub-horizon of the upper part of the B (read as its upper half): texture média with no macroaggregates and cerosidade of moderate grade; texture média with prismatic or blocky structure of moderate or strong grade and cerosidade of at least moderate grade; texture argilosa or muito argilosa with that structure and cerosidade at least common and weak or few and moderate; or a relação textural of 1.4 with a fragipã;
  • (j) across a discontinuity of parent material, or with only a ploughed layer above the B, items (h) or (i) are needed.

A profile with no horizon designation at all (depth slices) cannot be read by these items and is tested as before, by the clay increase between layers. In the morphological mode a “t” in the designation of a B horizon stands for the B textural the data do not show, now with a material number in front too (“IIBt”).

The B latossólico

Texture francoarenosa or finer, less than 17 cmolc per kg of clay, cerosidade at most few and weak (item h, layer by layer; a range counts by its upper end), in B horizons where the designations are recorded, and 50 cm of the horizon: of the adjoining sub-horizons that meet those requirements, taken together (test_minimum_thickness(adjoining = TRUE)). The layers of a B textural are no B latossólico. A plinthic or gleyic horizon or a B nítico in the profile exclude it as before.

The Latossolos step asks that no B textural lie above the B latossólico: “o primeiro horizonte diagnóstico de subsuperfície, a contar da superfície, tem prevalência” (Cap. 4, p. 110), so that a thick BC of low-activity clay below a B textural makes no Latossolo.

B_incipiente() excludes the layers of this B textural and of this B latossólico (item a, p. 60); it excluded those of the WRB argic and ferralic horizons (30 cm, 16 cmolc). carater_latossolico() looks for the B latossólico below the sub-horizons that carry the evidence of the B textural. neossolo() no longer sets a diagnostic B aside: the B textural is looked for in B horizons, and the canonical Fluvisol has none.

argic_with_strong_clay_films() and audit_argic_strong_films() are kept as tools; the key no longer uses their rule.

The SiBCS B textural no longer goes through argic(), so that options(soilKey.diagnostic_engine = "aqp") does not change it, nor does the inference from “Bt” with clay films that the engine bundled (in the RJ file the reference Argissolos agreed were 181 with that engine and are 168 with either now). The engine still gives the B latossólico its limit of 20 cmolc and its fallbacks; a “t” the data do not show is read by the morphological mode.

soilKey 0.9.240 (2026-10-13)

SiBCS key: the “(B)” of the old horizon notation is read as the B incipiente it names

Until 1988 the B incipiente was written “(B)” in Brazil: “A (B) C”, “A1 (B)1 (B)2 C”, “A II(B)21 II(B)22”. Larach et al. (1988, “Definição e notação de horizontes e camadas do solo”, the reference of SiBCS 2018 for the notation) replaced it by “Bi”, which the book uses (“O horizonte B incipiente (Bi)”, Cap. 3). B_incipiente() takes its candidate layers from the designation, and .desg_master(), which every SiBCS test of the master horizon reads, left “(B)” as written: for the key it was not a B horizon. In the national BDsolos export 552 layers of 333 profiles carry it, and 293 of them are among the 640 profiles whose reference order is Cambissolos. With no diagnostic B found, they were keyed Neossolos.

.desg_master() now reads “(B)”, “(B)21”, “(B1)” and “II(B)22” as “Bi”, “Bi21”, “Bi1” and “Bi22”. The horizon data keep the designation as written, and a parenthesis that does not open the designation (“A3/(B)”, “B(2)”) is left alone. Nothing else of the B incipiente changes: the layer still has to be 10 cm thick and not to be a B textural, latossólico, espódico or plânico, so that a “(B)” that the data show to be a B latossólico is one. The reader serves the SiBCS key only; WRB and USDA read the designation by patterns of their own and are not touched.

The 8 that leave their reference are profiles labelled Neossolos (six of them by the old names Solo Litólico and Solo Aluvial) with a “(B)” of 10 cm or more, which by the book is a B incipiente: “Admitem um horizonte B em início de formação, cuja espessura não satisfaz a nenhum tipo de horizonte B diagnóstico” (Neossolos Litólicos, Cap. 12).

Panel of the EJSS article (798 profiles): 367 to 387 in the default mode and 489 to 507 in the morphological mode; only the row of the reference Cambissolos moves (15 to 35 agreed in the default mode). FEBR (1,000) keeps its confusion matrices (387 and 498 agreed) and no profile of Redape (94) changes (69 and 74). The 44 canonical profiles keep their class in the three systems, in both modes.

  • The export has a column “Tipo” that the loader does not read: of the 7,593 profiles with a reference order, 4,674 are “Perfil completo”, 332 “Perfil parcial” and 2,587 “Amostra extra”, in most cases two sampled layers, often with a gap between them. The order agreement of the three groups is 54.7%, 34.9% and 35.1% in the default mode.

    1. of the book; items (f), (g) and (i) are not tested, and the B latossólico does not exclude the B textural.

soilKey 0.9.239 (2026-10-12)

SiBCS key: the glei horizon is read by the colours of the book, with the drainage class as the record of its saturation

horizonte_glei() was the WRB test of gleyic properties under another name: redoximorphic features of 5% or more in a layer that starts within 50 cm, with no colour asked. A mottled Argissolo was a Gleissolo, and a grey Cg with no amount of mottles recorded was not. In the national BDsolos export the key called 468 profiles Gleissolos, of which 123 had that reference, and 141 reference Gleissolos were keyed Neossolos.

The book (SiBCS 2018, Cap. 2, p. 70-71): “o horizonte glei é um horizonte mineral, com espessura mínima de 15 cm, com menos de 15% de plintita e é saturado com água por influência do lençol freático durante algum período ou o ano todo […], apresentando evidências de processos de redução, com ou sem segregação de ferro, caracterizadas por um ou mais dos seguintes requisitos”: (a) the dominant colour, by four items; (b) “Coloração variegada com pelo menos uma das cores de acordo com um dos itens anteriores”; (c) reduced iron shown by a field test.

  • Colours. A layer qualifies by item (a1), neutral or bluer than 10Y; (a2), hues redder than 5YR with value 4 or more and chroma 1 or less; (a3), hues 5YR or yellower with value 4 or more and chroma 2 or less, or 3 in a hue 10YR or yellower when the chroma decreases in the horizon below; (a4), any hue and value with chroma 2 or less and mottles; or (b), a variegated layer (variegated_colors) with one colour of those items. Organic layers and layers with 15% of plinthite or more do not qualify. Item (c) is recorded by no profile.
  • Saturation. It is not measured. What a survey records of it is the drainage class of the site, and Anexo B (p. 315) describes the classes: in a “mal drenado” soil “o lençol freático comumente está à superfície ou próximo dela durante uma considerável parte do ano”, while an “imperfeitamente drenado” one shows “indícios de gleização nos seus horizontes mais profundos”. The colours make a glei horizon when the site is “mal drenado” or “muito mal drenado”. A class written as a range counts by its wetter end (“imperfeitamente a mal drenado” is “mal drenado”), an exception to the rule that a range is read by its lower end. The field is read as site$drainage (the BDsolos loader) or site$drainage_class.
  • No drainage class recorded. The layer itself has to show the saturation, beside its colours: mottles (“O horizonte sendo saturado com água periodicamente ou o solo tendo sido drenado deve apresentar algum mosqueado”, p. 70), a colour of item (a1), or a variegated colour. Without that, the greyish A and the pale E of any soil satisfy item (a3).
  • Morphological mode. The “g” of a designation (Cg, Btg) stands for the colours and for the saturation, as before.
  • Gleissolos (key, Cap. 4, p. 112-113): the glei horizon within 50 cm, or between 50 and 150 cm “desde que imediatamente subjacente a horizontes A ou E ou a horizonte hístico com menos de 40 cm de espessura”. Any glei horizon within 150 cm used to count.
  • Neossolos (p. 111): “Ausência de horizonte glei dentro de 50 cm a partir da superfície, exceto no caso de solos de textura areia e areia franca”. 150 cm was tested, with no exception.

The new internals are .glei_colour_item(), .glei_colour_layers(), .drainage_class() and .textura_areia_ou_areia_franca(). The WRB test, gleyic_properties(), is not changed.

soilKey 0.9.238 (2026-10-12)

SiBCS key: the B plânico is tested for its structure and for the colours of a variegated or mottled horizon

SiBCS 2018 (Cap. 2, p. 65-66) describes the B plânico by more than the key tested. It “Apresenta estrutura prismática, colunar ou em blocos angulares e subangulares grandes ou médios e, às vezes, estrutura maciça”, and its colours “devem atender a pelo menos um dos seguintes requisitos”: (a) the matrix colour; (b) “Coloração variegada com pelo menos uma cor apresentando matiz e croma conforme especificado no item (a)”; (c) “matiz 10YR ou mais amarelo, cromas ≥ 4, combinado com mosqueado de croma conforme especificado no item (a)”. B_planico() tested an abrupt textural change and item (a). A B horizon with small subangular blocks was a B plânico, and a variegated one, which has no matrix colour, was none.

  • Structure. Where the sheet records it, the structure has to be one of those the definition describes: prismatic, columnar or massive; or blocks, angular or subangular, that are medium or larger. A size written as a range is read by its lower end (“Pequena a média” is small), as the other minima are. A structure that is not recorded passes, and so do blocks with no size. The new internal .structure_size_class() reads the size in both languages.
  • Item (b) reads variegated_colors, and item (c) mottle_colors: a matrix of hue 10YR or yellower and chroma 4 or more, with a mottle whose colour satisfies item (a).

Of the reference Planossolos of the national BDsolos export that have a B plânico and a recorded structure, 84 of 90 have one of the list; the six that do not are in small blocks.

soilKey 0.9.237 (2026-10-12)

Redape and SmartSolos: the structure codes are read on the scales the service documents

The GeoTab files of Redape, and the SmartSolos Expert service they were made for, record the soil structure as integer codes. The service describes them (https://www.agroapi.cnptia.embrapa.br/store/api-docs/agroapi/SmartSolosExpert/v1):

Field Description
ESTRUTURA_GRAU “de ausente (1) a forte (4)”
ESTRUTURA_TAMANHO “de muito pequeno (1) a extremamente grande (6)”
ESTRUTURA_TIPO “laminar (1), prismática (2), colunar (3), blocos angulares (4), blocos subangulares (5), granular (6), grumosa (7)”

Since 0.9.189 the Redape loader read the grade on a scale of three (“weak” for 1) and the type in another order (“granular” for 1, “columnar” for 5). Of the 444 horizons of the 94 profiles: the 137 with subangular blocks were read as columnar, the 79 with angular blocks as prismatic, the 63 granular ones as platy; the 211 of weak grade were read as moderate, the 73 moderate ones as strong, and the 24 strong ones had no grade at all. The encoders that send a profile to the service (classify_via_smartsolos_api(), since 0.9.54) made the same two mistakes the other way round.

  • load_redape_pedons() decodes the three fields on the documented scales. A grade of 1 is “structureless”, a size of 6 “extremely coarse”, a type of 7 “crumb”.
  • The payload sent to the service encodes them on the same scales, so that what the loader decodes the encoder sends back as the same code.
  • A structure recorded as absent is now a grade below weak. It was read as not recorded, which passes a minimum such as the “grau moderado ou forte” of the B nítico. No profile of Redape or BDsolos records one.

The documented scales were checked against the data: 35 horizons of 7 Redape profiles are also in the BDsolos export, which keeps the words of the field sheet. Code 5 is “Blocos subangulares” there in 18 of 18 horizons, 6 is “Granular” in 6 of 6, 2 is “Prismática” in the one case; grade 2 is “Fraca” in 20 of 22 and grade 3 “Moderada” in 6 of 7.

CEROSIDADE_GRAU is described the same way, “de ausente (1) a forte (4)”, and is left on the scale of three it was read with (1 weak, 2 moderate, 3 strong). The files hold 1, 2 and 3 only, and 1 comes with an amount of clay films in 12 of 13 horizons, which “ausente” would not; no shared profile records clay films to settle it. It is an open question for the authors of the files.

Effect

  • Redape (94 profiles): 68 to 69 in the default mode and 72 to 73 in the morphological mode. The profile is GeoTab_PE_045_Cabo_de_Santo_Agostinho, a reference Nitossolos whose B horizons are in subangular blocks of moderate grade (codes 5 and 3). Read as columnar, they failed the structure of the B nítico, and the profile was keyed Latossolos, or Argissolos in the morphological mode. The Redape figures reported from 0.9.189 to 0.9.235 were computed with the structure read the old way.
  • The national BDsolos export (7,593 profiles), its panel of the EJSS article and FEBR do not change, in either mode: they do not go through these codes. The 44 canonical fixtures keep their class in the three systems.
  • The service itself was not called to verify the encoders; they follow its published description.

soilKey 0.9.235 (2026-10-12)

SiBCS key: the variegated colours and the colours of the mottles are read in the depth rule of Plintossolos

A plinthic horizon that starts below 40 cm makes a Plintossolo when it lies immediately below a horizon “que apresente cores pálidas, variegadas ou com mosqueados em quantidade abundante” (SiBCS 2018, Cap. 3, p. 104). Since 0.9.234 the key tested the pale colour and the amount of the mottles. It could not test the rest, because a profile held one colour per horizon: a variegated horizon, which has no single matrix colour, reached the key with no colour at all, and the mottles counted by their amount whatever their colour.

  • Two new columns of the profile, variegated_colors and mottle_colors: the Munsell notations the field sheet lists, separated by “;” ("10YR 5/3; 2.5YR 4/6"). They are in horizon_column_spec(), in the JSON schema of the profile and in inst/ATTRIBUTES.md, and are read only when present.
  • BDsolos loader. The export has “Variegado - Matiz / Valor / Croma” and “Mosqueado - Matiz / Valor / Croma”, each cell listing one entry per colour separated by “:” (“10YR:5YR”, “6:5”, “3:6”). They are joined into the notations. In the national export, 975 horizons of 654 profiles are variegated (947 of them have no matrix colour) and 2,649 horizons of 1,395 profiles have the colours of their mottles.
  • Redape loader. GeoTab gives up to three more colours in COR_MOSQ_*. Beside a matrix colour they are read as the colours of the mottles (15 horizons); in a horizon with no matrix colour, as its variegated colours (7 horizons of 4 profiles).
  • The rule, in the internal .plinthic_preceded(), with the two items the three kinds of colour answer to (“a) Matiz 5Y; ou b) Matizes 7,5YR, 10YR ou 2,5Y com croma menor ou igual a 4”) in the new internal .plintossolo_items_a_b():
    • variegated: “pelo menos uma das cores deve satisfazer aos itens (a) e (b)”. Hue and chroma only, as the book writes; the moist value of 5 or more that 0.9.234 asks of a pale matrix colour is not asked here. No profile of BDsolos or Redape differs between the two readings.
    • mottles: “deverão ocorrer em quantidade abundante (> 20% em volume) numa matriz de coloração avermelhada ou amarelada e deverão apresentar matizes e cromas conforme os itens (a) e (b)”. The amount is asked as before; the colour, of at least one of the mottles, when the sheet records it. A horizon with abundant mottles and no colour recorded passes as before. The colour of the matrix is not tested: the book gives no hue for “avermelhada ou amarelada”.

Effect

The 44 canonical fixtures keep their class in the three systems, in the default and in the morphological mode. Reloaded with the new loader, each of the 7,714 profiles of the national BDsolos export is identical to the one of 0.9.234 in every column that existed.

National BDsolos export, 7,593 profiles with a reference order. In the default mode no profile changes (3,349; the export records no volume of plinthite). In the morphological mode:

soilKey 0.9.234 (2026-10-12)

SiBCS key: the morphological mode reads “v” and “pl”, and a Plintossolo needs its plinthic horizon where the book says

The morphological mode (options(soilKey.morphological_inference = TRUE)) lets a horizon designation stand for a diagnostic the data cannot test. Two letters of the Brazilian notation were not read by it, and reading one of them brought out a rule that was looser than the book.

  • “v”, vertic features (Bv, Cv, Biv). vertic_horizon() reads the suffix only under an option of its own, because it also serves WRB and USDA, where “v” is plinthite (KST, FAO). horizonte_vertico(), the SiBCS wrapper, now turns that reading on in the morphological mode. For WRB and USDA nothing changes.
  • “pl”, plinthite in the older surveys (B21pl, Cpl), where “f” is written today. horizonte_plintico() reads it in the morphological mode, with the thickness it asks of “f”. Of the 331 profiles of the national BDsolos export whose reference order is Plintossolos, 80 carry “pl” and 64 carry “f”.
  • Where the plinthic horizon starts. plintossolo() accepted a plinthic, litoplinthic or concretionary horizon that started anywhere within 200 cm. The definition (SiBCS 2018, Cap. 3, p. 104; key, Cap. 4, p. 113) accepts it within 40 cm, or within 200 cm only “quando precedidos de horizonte glei ou situados imediatamente abaixo do horizonte A ou E ou de outro horizonte que apresente cores pálidas, variegadas ou com mosqueados em quantidade abundante”. The new internal .plinthic_preceded() tests that: a glei horizon above; or, in the horizon immediately above, an A or an E, mottles in abundant amount (more than 20%), or a pale colour. For the pale colour the book gives the hue and the chroma (5Y; or 7.5YR, 10YR or 2.5Y with chroma 4 or less) and no number for the lightness; a moist value of 5 or more is taken, so that a brown 10YR 4/4 is not pale. Variegated colours are not recorded and not tested.
  • Cambissolos. cambissolo() excluded a profile with any plinthic horizon, at any depth. The book excludes the ones that meet “os requisitos estabelecidos para serem enquadrados” as Plintossolos (Cap. 3, p. 88); the test now asks plintossolo().
  • The canonical Plintossolo. make_plintossolo_canonical() reuses the WRB fixture, whose plinthic horizons are written “Btv” and “Cv”. In the Brazilian notation that “v” is vertic, and the Brazilian “f” is frozen soil for KST and FAO. The profile is classified by the three keys (it is one of the demonstration profiles of the app), so its horizons are now “A”, “Bt”, “C”, with the plinthite it has measured. Its class does not change in any of the three systems.

In the default mode, no profile of the national BDsolos export changes order (the export records no volume of plinthite). The 44 canonical fixtures keep their class in the three systems.

soilKey 0.9.233 (2026-10-12)

SiBCS key: the colour of the B plânico is the one the book lists

SiBCS 2018 (Cap. 2, p. 65-66) asks of a B plânico a matrix colour of “Matiz 10YR ou mais amarelo, cromas ≤ 3” or of “Matizes 7,5YR ou 5YR, cromas ≤ 2”. B_planico() tested the first with the pattern 10YR|2\.5Y|5Y, which “5YR”, “7.5YR” and “2.5YR” also match, because all three contain “5Y”. A B horizon of hue 5YR or 7.5YR passed with chroma 3, and one of hue 2.5YR passed at all.

  • The hue is now read as a number and a family by the new internal .munsell_hue_parts() (“7.5YR” and “7,5YR” are 7.5 and “YR”). 10YR and the Y hues pass with chroma 3 or less; from 5YR up to, not including, 10YR, with chroma 2 or less; a redder hue does not pass.
  • Neutral and gley hues (N, GY, G, B) are not among the requirements the book lists and do not pass, as before.

The alternatives (b) and (c) of the book, a variegated colour and a matrix of chroma 4 or more with mottles of low chroma, need the colours of the mottles, which the profiles do not carry; they are not tested, as before.

The 44 canonical fixtures keep their class in the three systems.

On the national BDsolos export (7,593 profiles with a reference order), nineteen profiles change order in the default mode: seven now agree with their reference, six no longer do and six go from one disagreeing order to another. Order agreement 3,348 to 3,349; reference Planossolos agreed 95 to 91, Chernossolos 26 to 29, Argissolos 1,180 to 1,182. In the morphological mode, 3,854 to 3,855.

soilKey 0.9.231 (2026-10-12)

SiBCS key: in the B nítico, a grade written as a range is read by its lower end

SiBCS 2018 states the criteria of the B nítico as minima: structure “de grau de desenvolvimento moderado ou forte”, cerosidade “em quantidade no mínimo comum e com grau forte ou moderado” (Cap. 2, p. 61-62). A range meets a minimum only if all of it does. The amount of cerosidade has been read that way since 0.9.227 (“Pouca a comum” is below “comum”); the two grades were read with the pattern moder|strong|forte, which “Fraca a moderada” matches.

  • The new internal .grade_class() reads a grade of development on the scale weak / fraca, moderate / moderada, strong / forte, in English or Portuguese, and a range by its lower end. B_nitico() uses it for the grade of the structure and for the grade of the cerosidade. “Moderada a forte” passes; “Fraca a moderada” and “weak to moderate” do not. A grade that was not recorded does not fail the layer, as before.

The other kind of criterion is a maximum, and there a range counts by its upper end: the B latossólico admits “no máximo cerosidade pouca e fraca” (p. 58-59), so “Pouca a comum” exceeds it. The clay-film gate of the B latossólico already reads it so and is not changed.

The 44 canonical fixtures keep their class in the three systems.

On the national BDsolos export (7,593 profiles with a reference order), default mode, seven profiles change order: two reference Nitossolos are no longer reached (PR 6654, SC 11902), two reference Argissolos are no longer keyed Nitossolos and agree (MT 6184, MT 10801), one reference Argissolos goes from Argissolos to Neossolos (MG 5916), and two go from one disagreeing order to another. soilKey 0.9.229 (2026-10-11)

SiBCS benchmarks: a label is read by what it states, when that places it in another order

The label map read every “Podzólico” as Argissolos and every “Cambissolo” as Cambissolos. Anexo I of SiBCS 2018 (p. 342) is finer, and three kinds of label state attributes that the book places in another order than their name. The new internal .sibcs_stated_order() reads them, after the order of the name.

  • Podzólico Vermelho-Amarelo or Vermelho-Escuro that states Eutrófico and high-activity clay (“Ta”, “argila de atividade alta”) is Luvissolos: Anexo I lists the “Podzólicos Vermelho-Amarelos Eutróficos Ta” and the “Podzólicos Vermelho-Escuros Eutróficos Ta” under Luvissolos. 31 labels of the national BDsolos export. The “Podzólicos Amarelos” are Argissolos in Anexo I without condition and stay so.
  • A label that begins with “Argissolo” and states Eutrófico and high-activity clay is read as Luvissolos. Such a label contradicts itself: an Argissolo has a B textural “de argila de atividade baixa, ou atividade alta desde que conjugada com saturação por bases baixa ou com caráter alumínico” (p. 87), and a B textural with high-activity clay and high base saturation is a Luvissolo (p. 95). The 36 labels of this kind, 19 of them from Acre (“ARGISSOLO VERMELHO-AMARELO Eutrófico argila de atividade alta A moderado textura argilosa.”), read as the old Podzólico names with the first word replaced. The attributes stated are taken, not the word.
  • Cambissolo in the old form that states Eutrófico, high-activity clay and A chernozêmico is Chernossolos: the exception of Anexo I (“exceto os Cambissolos Eutróficos com horizonte A chernozêmico e com argila de atividade alta”). 11 labels. A label whose second word is a present suborder (“CAMBISSOLO HÁPLICO Eutrófico Ta A chernozêmico”, 2 labels) was written in SiBCS and is left as it is.

“Eutrófico” is the word itself: “Epieutrófico” and the like do not count. A label that states both “Ta” and “Tb” keeps the order of its name.

Left as they were, on purpose:

  • the 52 “Podzólico … Eutrófico” or “Equivalente Eutrófico” labels that do not state the clay activity: the book places them in Luvissolos if Ta and in Argissolos if Tb, and the label does not say;
  • the “plíntico” labels under Podzólico (93), Latossolo (32) and Glei (4): the book sends “parte” or “alguns” of them to Plintossolos;
  • the Podzólicos Vermelho-Escuros Tb (51), “alguns” of which the book sends to Nitossolos.

49 of the 78 profiles now agree with their reference. 7 no longer do: they are among the 36 “Argissolo” labels, and the key returns Argissolos for them. None of the 42 Podzólico and Cambissolo profiles agreed before.

soilKey 0.9.228 (2026-10-11)

SiBCS key: a horizon is read without the number of its material

A horizon below a lithologic discontinuity is written with the number of its material in front: “2Bt1” today, “IIBt1” in the surveys that numbered the materials in Roman numerals. The SiBCS diagnostics chose their horizons with patterns such as ^B and ^A, which neither form matches, so a “IIBt” was not a B horizon for them. In the national BDsolos export 1,984 horizons of 874 profiles carry such a number, 670 of them B horizons. The clearest loss was in Planossolos, whose B plânico is very often the top of a second material (“A1 A3 IIBt IIC”): the abrupt textural change passed in 186 of the 291 profiles with that reference order and the B plânico in 56.

  • The new internal .desg_master() gives a designation without the number of the material, Arabic or Roman (“2Bt1” and “IIBt1” are “Bt1”). The 56 designation patterns of the SiBCS diagnostics, in 39 functions of the order, suborder, attribute and family levels, now read it. All of them ask whether a horizon is a B, an A, a C, an R or an O, or a B with some suffix; none looks for the number. The horizon data keep the designation as written.
  • Three of those functions already accepted an Arabic number (^[0-9]*A) but not a Roman one.

The canonical fixtures have no numbered horizon and classify as before. Their SiBCS order no longer depends on the number: with the subsoil of each fixture written as a second material (“II” or “2” in front of its horizons), 18 of the 44 changed order before this version (the canonical Planossolo became Gleissolos, the Luvissolo Argissolos) and none does now.

soilKey 0.9.227 (2026-10-11)

SiBCS key: the B nítico test reads cerosidade and structure in the language of the field sheet

SiBCS 2018 (Cap. 2, p. 61-62) asks of a B nítico “cerosidade em quantidade no mínimo comum e com grau forte ou moderado” and “estrutura em blocos ou prismática”. B_nitico() compared clay_films_amount with the literal English terms c("common", "many", "abundant", "strong"). The BDsolos export words the amount as the Brazilian field sheets do (“Comum” in 1,218 horizons, “Pouca” in 874, “Abundante” in 523), so the criterion passed in none of its profiles: of the 7,694 labelled profiles of the national export, classify_sibcs() returned Nitossolos for none, although 145 of the 347 whose reference order is Nitossolos record cerosidade “comum” or more and “moderada” or more.

  • The amount is now read on the ordinal scale of .clay_films_class() (none, few / pouca, common / comum, many or abundant / abundante), the reader the WRB nitic horizon already used, in English or Portuguese and whatever the case. min_cerosidade keeps its default; its lowest term sets the threshold, and a term the scale does not know passes only if it is listed, as before.
  • A range of amounts is read by its lower end: “Pouca a comum” is below “comum”, “Comum a abundante” meets it.
  • The type of structure is matched without depending on accents: “Prismática” and “Prismática que se desfaz” (789 horizons of the export) did not match the pattern prismatic|prismatica. The new internal .field_term() gives a field term in lower case and without accents.

Profiles described with the English terms are read exactly as before: the 44 canonical fixtures keep their class in the three systems, and their SiBCS order is now the same when their terms are written in Portuguese.

On the national BDsolos export (7,593 profiles with a reference order), default mode:

soilKey 0.9.226 (2026-10-11)

SiBCS benchmarks: the old soil names of the reference labels are read as their present-day order

0.9.225 left out of the scored profiles every reference label whose first word is not an order of SiBCS 5. Most of those labels are names of the classifications in use before SiBCS: 876 of the 7,694 labels of the national BDsolos export, counting the 252 that begin with “Solo” or “Solos”. The 5th edition (Santos et al., 2018) says where each old class went, in the “Abrangência” paragraph of each order (chapter 3, p. 87 to 106) and in its Anexo I (p. 342). normalise_febr_sibcs() now follows it.

  • Names the book gives to one order are in .SIBCS_LEGACY_ORDER_MAP: Latosol (Latossolos), Planosol and Solonetz-Solodizado (Planossolos), Brunizem and Rendzina (Chernossolos), Regossolo, Litosol and Solos Litólicos (Neossolos), Solos Orgânicos (Organossolos), Vertisol (Vertissolos), Cambisol (Cambissolos), Solos Concrecionários and Concrecionários Lateríticos (Plintossolos), Rubrozem (Argissolos), with the misspellings of these and of the present orders found in the export (“PLITOSSOLO”, “NEO0SSOLO”, “POZDÓLICO”, “ARE1A QUARTZOSA”). 628 labels.
  • Names that take two words are in the new .SIBCS_LEGACY_TWO_WORD_MAP: Bruno Não Cálcico (Luvissolos), Humic Glei and Low-Humic Glei (Gleissolos), Solos Indiscriminados Concrecionários (Plintossolos), and Terra Roxa and Terra Bruna Estruturada (Nitossolos). For the last two the book says “na maioria” (p. 98), with a “pequena parte” in Argissolos (p. 87); the name does not say which, and the 147 labels are read as the majority.
  • “Solo” or “Solos” in front is not the name: the word after it is (“SOLO LITÓLICO” is Neossolos, “SOLOS ORGÂNICOS” Organossolos). A “Solos …” label followed by no name of the maps is NA, as before.
  • A hyphen separates the words of a name as a space does (“LATOSSOLO-VERMELHO”, “SOLONETZ-SOLODIZADO”).

These readings are tried only when the first word gives no order, so a label that was read before is read the same.

Left out on purpose, and still NA (101 labels):

  • names the book divides between orders by something the name does not say: Hidromórfico Cinzento (Gleissolos without an abrupt textural change, Planossolos with one), Solonchak (Gleissolos only with a glei horizon), Alissolo;
  • names that are not in its correlation: Laterítico Bruno Avermelhado (which is not Laterita Hidromórfica), Solos Brunos Ácidos, Solos Coluviais, Mediterrâneo Vermelho-Amarelo;
  • labels that begin with a Soil Taxonomy name (“Typic Haplorthox ou Latossolo …”), “aterro”, and the labels the database itself marks as doubtful (“*MUDAR*”, “*CORRIGIR*”).

soilKey 0.9.225 (2026-10-11)

SiBCS benchmarks: a reference label counts only if it is a SiBCS order

  • Punctuation around the first word is dropped first, so “ESPODOSSOLO.”, “Vertissolo.” and “PLANOSSOLO(???)” are read as their orders.

soilKey 0.9.224 (2026-10-10)

Pro app: every instance serves the scripts a drawn widget brings

The Map tab could come up as a grey box, without base map or overlay, when Cloud Run had a second instance up. A map with provider tiles brings two scripts when it is drawn, the provider list and leaflet’s plugin for it. They are not in the page, so the start-up registration of 0.9.215 left them out. Shiny registered them only in the R process that drew a map, and a request routed to another instance got HTTP 404. Seen on 2026-10-10 in the request logs of the live 0.9.222 and of a 0.9.223 test revision, with two sessions open at once: page and websocket on one instance, the two 404s on another.

A local run through every tab, with each resource path logged, found the same for two other widgets: DT’s DataTables core and plotly’s plotly.js bundle are registered when the first table or plot is drawn. No 404 was seen for those.

  • sk_register_widget_deps(), called at start-up after the page is rendered, registers what a table, a plot and a map with provider tiles bring: 34 prefixes at start-up in the local run, against 28. Only prefixes that are not registered yet are added, so nothing of the page is re-pointed, and a widget’s own jQuery is left out.
  • Maps and map proxies get their provider tiles through sk_provider_tiles().
  • A provider list in the temporary folder is never served from there. Shiny serves the folder a dependency is in, whole, and leaflet has a fallback that writes the provider list to the R session’s temporary folder; sk_own_dependency() moves such a dependency to a folder that holds only its files. The container image does not take that fallback: there the list comes from the installed leaflet.providers package folder, so no temporary folder was served by the live app. (This note first said it was; a check inside the 0.9.224 image showed otherwise.)

Checked in a fresh local process, before any session: the two provider scripts answered 404 and now answer 200. In a session through every tab no prefix is re-pointed, and the only new one is the jQuery of plotly’s crosstalk, which the browser does not ask for (the page’s jQuery is there). The base map loads and changes with the selector.

Checked on the container image: a fresh instance of 0.9.223 answered 404 for the five draw-time scripts before any session (the two provider scripts, the DataTables core, plotly.js and typedarray), and one of 0.9.224 answers 200. Four sessions at once, over three instances, drew every map, table and plot without a failed request.

soilKey 0.9.223 (2026-10-10)

The AfSP row of the benchmark suite

run_all_benchmarks() has a row for the AfSP sample (WRB, Africa), and it was never there. load_afsp_sample() returns a list that holds the 120 profiles in $pedons, beside the date, source and filter of the snapshot. The suite cut that whole list to max_n and handed it to benchmark_afsp(), which stopped with “$ operator is invalid for atomic vectors”. The suite dropped the error and went on without the row, and without a word (seen in 0.9.187 and 0.9.222).

  • benchmark_afsp() takes the list load_afsp_sample() returns, or its $pedons. Anything that is not a list of PedonRecord objects is refused with a message that says so.
  • The suite scores the sample’s profiles and applies max_n to them. With the sample cached, the summary has the row: n = 120, RSG agreement 25.0% [17.5, 32.5], kappa 0.218 in the strict mode.
  • A sample that is present but cannot be scored is reported (“AfSP sample present but could not be scored: …”). An absent sample is skipped as before, with a note when verbose = TRUE.
  • The help of load_afsp_sample() said 130 profiles over 26 RSGs. The sample has 120 over 24.

It went unseen because the AfSP tests only run with the sample in inst/extdata, and the suite test asked for “only the canonical row”, which the missing row satisfied. That test now accepts the AfSP row, and the new tests use a three-profile stand-in for the sample.

soilKey 0.9.222 (2026-10-10)

BDsolos: every export read by one reader; loading several files no longer hangs

load_bdsolos_csv() read each file with data.table::fread() and fell back to utils::read.csv2() when that failed. The export quotes every field. Its free-text fields hold line breaks and, in 11 of the 27 state files of the national export, quotation marks of their own (formação "Camaquã"). On those files fread() did one of two things:

  • It split the records at the line breaks, with a warning the loader silenced. BA, GO, PI and RS were read this way: RS gave 3,853 rows for its 897 records. Lines of text became profiles of their own, 1,281 of the 8,995 “profiles” of the national export (553 in BA, 248 in GO, 69 in PI, 411 in RS), and the real profiles of those states got broken horizons and, often, no reference class.
  • It stopped with “attempt to set index N/N in SET_STRING_ELT” (DF, MT, PA, PB, SP). The loader then used read.csv2(), which read the file right. But the error came from inside an OpenMP critical section of fread(), which stayed locked: the next fread() of the R session never returned. Loading the state files in a loop, as benchmark_unified() and the download_bdsolos() example do, hung at the first file after DF (data.table 1.18.4).

read.csv2() now reads every file (.bdsolos_read_table()), and the loader no longer calls fread(). Checked against the export’s own structure, where a record ends with "; at the end of a line: the same 8,550,304 cells in the 27 files, except that it drops the quotation marks inside 231 text fields. The 27 files load in one R session, with the same result as one session per file.

What changes in the loaded data:

  • The national export has 7,714 profiles, not 8,995.
  • BA, GO, PI and RS have 1,424 profiles (were 2,705) with 5,344 horizons (were 13,045). 1,373 of them have a SiBCS reference class (were 1,017), and the SiBCS order agrees with it in 33.5% (was 20.5%).
  • DF, MT, PA, PB, PE, RN and SP are identical.
  • In the other 16 states the profiles and their numbers are the same, and an empty text field is now NA, as it already was in the 7 states above. It was "" (91,528 cells), which the keys took for a recorded value:
    • 56 profiles go from Regosols to Cambisols, and 56 (54 of them the same) from Entisols to Inceptisols (52) or Aridisols (4): a B horizon without a structure description (structure_grade of "") counted as structureless and failed the cambic horizon; it is now missing data;
    • 220 profiles without a Munsell hue got a colour suborder by default (Argissolos Vermelho-Amarelos 181, Latossolos Vermelho-Amarelos 22, Luvissolos Háplicos 17) and are now “(cor a determinar)”;
    • 54 other SiBCS names change, 3 of them in the order (Neossolos to Chernossolos), and 33 other WRB names in their qualifiers. The SiBCS order agreement of these states stays at 39.6%.
    • A line break inside a text field is \n; fread() kept the file’s \r\n (13 site fields).
  • Over the national export the SiBCS order agrees with the reference class in 38.6% (2,871 of 7,442 labelled profiles); it was 37.0% (2,619 of 7,086).

The loader’s comment blamed malformed UTF-8 for the fread() failures. The 27 files are valid UTF-8.

Earlier BDsolos figures in this file (8,995 profiles, n = 7,086) include the 1,281 lines of text read as profiles.

soilKey 0.9.221 (2026-10-08)

BDsolos and FEBR: dithionite Fe and sulfuric-attack Fe2O3 kept apart

Both loaders filled fe_dcb_pct, the dithionite (free) Fe that the WRB criteria read, with the Fe2O3 of the sulfuric attack, the total Fe as the oxide that the SiBCS férrico classes read. They also left it in g/kg, where soilKey stores %. So a BDsolos horizon with 43 g/kg Fe2O3 was recorded with 43% free Fe, and every horizon with a sulfuric attack passed the WRB Fe-dith limits (4% for the nitic horizon, 10% for Ferritic). This affects 23,021 layers of the national BDsolos export. fe2o3_sulfuric_pct stayed empty, so the SiBCS férrico and perférrico classes were never reached on these data.

  • load_bdsolos_csv(): “CDB - Ferro (g/kg)” goes to fe_dcb_pct, “Ataque sulfúrico - Fe2O3” to fe2o3_sulfuric_pct and “Oxalato de Amônio - Ferro” to fe_ox_pct, all converted from g/kg to %. The CDB column (667 layers) comes after the sulfuric one in the export, so it used to be dropped.
  • read_febr_pedons() follows the FEBR dictionary codes, all in g/kg:
    • ferro_ditionito_* (or fe2o3_ditionito_*, converted to the element) to fe_dcb_pct;
    • ferro_oxalato_* / fe2o3_oxalato_* to fe_ox_pct;
    • fe2o3_sulfurico_* (or ferro_sulfurico_*, converted to the oxide) to fe2o3_sulfuric_pct.
    Until now the first fe2o3_* column of any method filled fe_dcb_pct: sulfuric, aqua regia, oxalate or dithionite. The map also asked for a ferro_dcb code the dictionary does not have.
  • Readers that took the sulfuric Fe2O3 for dithionite Fe on these data: the WRB nitic horizon and the Ferric and Ferritic qualifiers; the SiBCS caráter espódico (Fe-dith >= 0.5%, so every B with a sulfuric attack passed that part); and the USDA Ferrudalfs (Fe-dith >= 4%).

On the national BDsolos export (8,995 profiles in the 27 state files), 6,654 profiles load with different Fe data. Classified before and after in the three systems, none changes RSG, SiBCS order or USDA order, and the SiBCS order agreement with their BDsolos labels stays at 36.5% (5,563 labelled). The names change:

  • WRB: Ferric falls from 2,298 names to 14. All 14 have CDB Fe; 7 of them get it through the CDB column that used to be dropped.
  • SiBCS: 129 names gain an iron class (94 Distroférricos, 10 Aluminoférricos, 10 Eutroférricos, 9 Férricos, 6 Perférricos). Of the 68 profiles whose BDsolos label has an iron class and whose sulfuric Fe2O3 reaches 18%, 42 are now named with one (none before). 11 profiles lose the espodossólico subgroup (Cambissolos and Neossolos).
  • USDA: Ferrudalfs fall from 403 to 6, all 6 with CDB Fe >= 4%. The others are now Paleudalfs, Kandiudalfs, Hapludalfs or Rhodudalfs.

Not changed: the REDAPE GeoTab loader maps TEOR_FE (values of 6-49, so g/kg) to fe_dcb_pct. The dataset does not say whether it is dithionite Fe or sulfuric Fe2O3, so it is left as it was until that is known. The sulfuric Al2O3 and SiO2 of BDsolos and FEBR (for Ki and Kr) are still not loaded.

soilKey 0.9.220 (2026-10-08)

WRB 2022 diagnostics checked against Chapter 3

The qualifier audit of 0.9.217 found diagnostics that also decide RSGs and did not follow their WRB 2022 definitions. Each now reads its criteria: a criterion is FALSE when the data contradict it and NA when the data it needs are missing. Of the 44 example profiles, 8 change WRB name and none changes RSG; one, the Retisol, also changes SiBCS and USDA class (below).

  • Nitic horizon (Ch 3.1.22), nitic_horizon():
    • the structure and shiny-faces criterion (2) now decides: blocky (moderate or strong) or polyhedral structure, and clay films (“cerosidade”) of “common” or more, the level the SiBCS B nitico asks for; until now it never vetoed;
    • Fe-ox >= 0.2% and Fe-ox / Fe-dith >= 0.05 (3) are read;
    • a layer of a plinthic horizon is excluded (4), so the example Plinthosols are no longer Nitic;
    • a ferralic horizon elsewhere in the profile no longer excludes it (Nitisols key out before Ferralsols);
    • the reading of legacy profiles added in 0.9.18 (a Bt designation, a CEC of 8-36 cmolc/kg clay and no albic E standing in for missing structure and Fe data) now runs only with options(soilKey.morphological_inference = TRUE), like the other designation-based readings.
  • Nitisols are keyed by the new nitisol(), the Chapter 4 entry: a nitic horizon starting <= 100 cm, a clay content above it at least half of its weighted average, no vertic horizon above it. It replaces a non-WRB veto on a clay drop of more than 8 percentage points within 50 cm.
    • The canonical Nitisol now records oxalate Fe (0.8-0.9%).
    • On the 219 FEBR profiles with a WRB class, which record no structure, clay films or Fe fractions, the 7 Nitisols keyed correctly all came from the default inference: RSG agreement goes from 22.0% to 19.3%.
    • With the option on it goes from 26.6% to 26.1%, still with 7 correct Nitisols, but not the same ones. Six that matched before fail the Chapter 4 clay rule (an A of 12-18% clay over a Bt of about 40%) or start below 100 cm, and six others now pass.
  • Continuous rock (Ch 3.2.5), continuous_rock() and the Leptosol gate:
    • R, RCr and R/Cr, also below a lithic discontinuity (2R);
    • Cr, weathered or soft bedrock, no longer counts. It is not continuous rock in WRB 2022 nor a contato litico in SiBCS 2018 (“rochas sas (camada R) … ou … majoritariamente por rocha dura (RCr ou R/Cr)”).
  • Technic hard material (Ch 3.3.18), technic_hard_material():
    • technic_hardmaterial_pct >= 95 or an asphalt or concrete designation;
    • any strongly cemented layer counted before, so a petrocalcic horizon or a duripan was technic, and so did a geomembrane.
  • Claric material (Ch 3.3.4), and the albic horizon that consists of it, need the dry and the moist colour; either was enough. The example Acrisol, Alisol, Lixisol and Luvisol lose Albic, and the Cryosol too: their E is 5/3 moist (claric) but 6/3 dry (not).
  • Argic horizon (Ch 3.1.3):
    • criterion 2.a.i: a clay increase over a coarser layer of another material (Ap over 2Bt) counts only with clay films of “common” or more (illuvial clay, criterion 2.b). WRB only: the SiBCS B textural, whose item (j) accepts such an increase by its textural ratio, and the USDA keys call argic(lithic_discontinuity = FALSE);
    • a glossic, albeluvic or retic designation no longer voids it, in any system. It was the WRB 2014 Albeluvisol logic; in WRB 2022 retic properties belong to an argic or natric horizon. The example Retisol gains Cutanic, Differentic, Epic and Profondic. In SiBCS it goes from Neossolos Regoliticos to Luvissolos Cromicos Orticos, and in USDA from Aeric Epiaquepts to Typic Albaqualfs: its Btg has twice the clay of the
  • Panpaic horizon (Ch 3.1.23), panpaic(), was any designation with a “b”, AB included (matched ignoring case). It is now a buried surface horizon (Ab, 2A) with >= 0.2% SOC, >= 25% and >= 0.2% more than the layer above, a lithic discontinuity at its upper limit, >= 5 cm; the Panpaic qualifier only adds the depth.
  • Retic properties (Ch 3.2.11), retic_properties(), need an argic or natric horizon (criterion 1) and the interfingering recorded at its upper limit (6); the designation stands in for the criteria no column holds.
  • Lamellic, qual_lamellic(), reads lamellae from the layers: 0.5-7.5 cm, more clay than the layers above and below (argic 2.a) or clay films, >= 5 cm together within 50 cm. A lamella designation alone gives NA.

Not changed here: argic criteria 2.a.ii-iii (plough layer, transitional horizon <= 15 cm) and the “minimum clay above” reference of the clay-increase test; lithic_discontinuity(), which reads a 10-point jump in coarse fragments; and the Leptosol path through coarse fragments (WRB: < 20% fine earth averaged over 75 cm).

soilKey 0.9.219 (2026-10-08)

  • Pro app: the navbar is the espresso brown of the theme in both colour modes. With the Flatly theme, bslib 0.7 (the container’s) paints a light navbar with the primary colour and a dark one with the success colour, and page_navbar() chooses between them from the theme current when the page is built. Until 0.9.218 that theme was unknown on an instance that had not served a page yet, so the navbar was brown or green depending on the instance; once 0.9.218 made it known everywhere, the navbar was green. soilkey.css now sets it.

soilKey 0.9.218 (2026-10-08)

Pro app: pages no longer lose jQuery or their theme after a table or a map

On the live app, an instance that had rendered a key-trace table or a map then served pages without jQuery (HTTP 404 for jquery-3.6.0/jquery.min.js), so they came up broken, until it was restarted. The page loads Shiny’s jQuery from the resource path jquery-3.6.0; DT and leaflet widgets also carry jquerylib’s jQuery, of the same version in the container’s Shiny 1.8, under the same path, and rendering one re-pointed it to a folder without jquery.min.js. Found in the request logs of the 0.9.218 test revision: one instance answered 200, then 404 from the moment a session there had rendered the table. sk_datatable() and the new sk_leaflet() drop the widgets’ own jQuery; the page’s is the one they use. A local install, on a newer Shiny (jQuery 3.7.1), never collides, which is why only the container showed it.

The same test revision showed a second fault, of the multi-instance setup of 0.9.215: a session that Cloud Run opened on an instance which had not yet served a page had no theme. Shiny records the theme when it serves a page with the app running, and app.R, where 0.9.215 renders the page at start-up, is sourced before that. Its tables then took DT’s default style, and selectize and bslib’s component CSS, rendered unthemed, re-pointed their resource paths to folders without the themed files, so pages that instance served next lost their select inputs’ and layout’s styles (404). sk_register_page_deps() now also makes the app’s theme the theme of every session from start-up.

Cloud Run’s session affinity is best effort, and the request with which a server-side DT table fetches its rows (/session/<id>/dataobj/<table>) could reach an instance that did not hold the session: the table stayed empty. The app’s tables are small, so they now send their rows with the table, over the session’s websocket (sk_renderDT(), server = FALSE).

Pro app: readable dark mode, AA contrast in both themes

A contrast check of every tab (WCAG 2.1 AA: 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for large text), in dark and in light mode, found 21 failing combinations of text and background in dark mode and 17 in light mode. All now pass; the only text under 4.5:1 left is the “Key” of the soilKey logotype, which WCAG exempts.

  • Assistant replies were unreadable in dark mode: light text on Bootstrap’s --bs-light, which stays near-white (1.0:1). Both chat bubbles now use the app palette: the reply on the sand wash, the question on the brown (it was white on light clay, 1.9:1 dark and 2.5:1 light).
  • The key trace “criteria” cells (met / not met / assigned / needs data) kept their light pastel fills under light text in dark mode (1.0-1.1:1). The fills are palette tokens now, with dark shades in dark mode; so are the probability colours of the Uncertainty table.
  • Plotly charts (depth profile, spectrum, posterior) were white panels in dark mode; they now draw on the card colour with light axis text and grid.
  • The terracotta accent is darkened from #B5652E to #9E5626 and the moss from #5E7B3B to #557036 (CSS palette and bs_theme()), so white text on them, and them as text on the light washes, reach 4.5:1 (buttons, links, the footer version, pre output, the inactive result tabs were 3.7-4.3:1).
  • Dark mode: terracotta buttons and the Assistant button take dark text (white on them was 2.4-2.6:1); outline buttons, .text-success and the “results are up to date” style notes take the dark-mode shades (they were 2.4-4.2:1); the profile picker is no longer a white box.
  • Both themes: “Skip tour” is a plain link (it was muted text on a terracotta button, 1.4-1.9:1); the table pager is brown, not Flatly’s green with near-white text (2.3:1); Docs in the navbar is styled like the other navbar links (1.6:1); the footer licence line is 5:1 (2.8:1); the grade C badge is a darker orange (white on it was 2.6:1).

soilKey 0.9.217 (2026-10-08)

WRB 2022 names follow WRB 2022: Chapter 4 lists, Chapter 2.2 rules

soilKey called its WRB names “WRB 2022”, but for most RSGs the qualifier lists were the longer WRB 2014 lists, and a list became a name by rules that were not WRB 2022’s. Both are now the text’s. 43 of the 44 example profiles change WRB name (the Neossolo, an Umbric Leptosol, keeps it); none changes RSG, and SiBCS and USDA names are untouched. Names cited from earlier versions (the README, papers) need updating: the example Ferralsol, for instance, was “Geric Ferric Rhodic Ferralsol (Clayic, Humic, Eutric, Ochric, Rubic)” and is now “Geric Rhodic Ferralsol (Clayic, Epic, Eutric, Ferric, Humic)”.

  • The 32 lists are Chapter 4’s. inst/rules/wrb2022/qualifiers.yaml is generated from the corrected text (18 December 2022) by data-raw/wrb2022_ch4_lists.py and data-raw/wrb2022_qualifiers_yaml.py: each RSG’s principal qualifiers in their ranked order and its supplementary ones, with alternatives kept as WRB writes them (“Rhodic/Xanthic”). Ferralsols had 29 principal qualifiers (Ferric, Hyperdystric, Plinthic, Histic and Vitric among them) against WRB 2022’s 13: Ferritic, Gibbsic, Rhodic/Xanthic, Geric, Nitic, Pretic, Gleyic, Stagnic, Profundihumic, Mollic/Umbric, Acric/Lixic, Skeletic, Haplic. Qualifiers that define the RSG (Chernic for Chernozems, Calcic for Calcisols, Plinthic for Plinthosols, Duric for Durisols, Stagnic for Planosols) are no longer in its own list.
  • The rules for naming soils (Chapter 2.2), in resolve_wrb_qualifiers():
    • principal qualifiers are written right to left, “the uppermost qualifier in the list is placed closest to the name of the RSG”;
    • supplementary qualifiers start with texture, then follow “the order of the alphabet”, by qualifier, not subqualifier (they kept the list order);
    • in a slash group only the first qualifier that applies is used (the example Ferralsol had both Humic and Ochric); every alternative is still evaluated and traced;
    • “Qualifiers conveying redundant information are not added … Eutric is not added if the Calcaric qualifier applies”, nor its subqualifiers (Hypereutric, Epieutric, Endoeutric), and likewise with Dolomitic;
    • Haplic, “no other principal qualifier of the respective RSG applies”, only where the RSG lists it: 16 RSGs do not (their last entry, e.g. Dystric/Eutric, applies to any soil with the data). A soil with no principal qualifier in such an RSG is still written with its supplementary ones (“Technosol (Loamic, Humic, Irragric, Mollic, Terric)”).
  • **A qualifier’s own function is tried before reading its name as specifier
    • qualifier.** Epic (ep) was read as Epi- + “c” and never evaluated.
  • Epic, Endic and Dorsic refer to “the uppermost respective diagnostic horizon of the RSG” (the ferralic horizon in a Ferralsol, the argic in a Luvisol, the cryic in a Cryosol) and now get the RSG from the resolver. Epic passed for any profile with a horizon starting above 50 cm, and Dorsic read a “ridge” microrelief field.
  • Novic, the one Chapter 4 qualifier without a function, is added (a 5-50 cm layer over a buried soil, read from the designation suffix b). coverage_report("wrb_qualifiers") is 234 of 234.

The qualifiers that now reach names were checked against Chapter 5

96 qualifiers of the WRB 2022 lists had never been in soilKey’s lists; their functions, written from the qualifier’s name in v0.9.63-64, now decide names. Each was compared with its Chapter 5 definition (and the diagnostic horizons, properties and materials it refers to): 68 were rewritten, 23 now return NA when soilKey holds no data for what the definition needs (and FALSE when the data rule it out), 5 were already right. A few of what they did:

  • Gibbsic took Al2O3 from sulfuric attack >= 25% for gibbsite >= 25%, which many clayey Ferralsols reach; it is now NA without a gibbsite figure.
  • Oxyaquic passed on >= 5% redox features without a gley colour; WRB 2022 asks for a saturated layer and “not having gleyic properties and not having stagnic properties” within 100 cm.
  • Epieutric passed on 29 of the 44 example profiles, ignoring “absent in the major part between 20 and 100 cm” (Ch 2.3.1, rule 3); Mineralic on 42, Neocambic on 18, Tonguic on 11 (any AB or BA horizon, or an irregular boundary) and Panpaic on 9 (the panpaic diagnostic read an AB horizon as buried).
  • Carbonic counted any organic carbon >= 5% (“that belongs to artefacts” in WRB 2022), Fractic any shrink-swell crack (remnants of a broken-up petro- horizon), Nechic any loess or dune description (uncoated grains in a darker matrix at pH < 5).
  • New in the example names: Differentic on the Acrisol, Alisol, Lixisol, Luvisol and Solonetz (“an argic or natric horizon that meets diagnostic criterion 2.a”; it passed on a clay ratio of 1.2-1.4 between any two horizons), Ferritic on the Nitisol, Hypernatric on the Solonetz, Pantofluvic on the Fluvisol.

Where the definition needs data soilKey cannot hold (soil-solution anions, gibbsite, uncoated grains, black carbon, subsurface water flow, …) the qualifier is never TRUE; each function’s comment quotes the definition and names what is missing.

Diagnostics and qualifiers corrected on the way

  • hydragric(): WRB 2022 Ch 3.1, criterion 1, the horizon “is overlain by an anthraquic horizon”. Any Bg/Brg/Bdg horizon of 20 cm passed (the example Gleysols and Stagnosol did), and Chapter 4 lists Hydragric for Gleysols and Stagnosols, so they would have been named as paddy soils.
  • Toxic: “toxic concentrations of organic or inorganic substances other than ions of Al, Fe, Na, Ca and Mg”. It passed on pH <= 3.5 or EC >= 16 dS/m, the acidity and salts the definition leaves out (the example Solonchak passed; Chapter 4 lists Toxic for every RSG but Chernozems, Kastanozems and Phaeozems). It now needs a recorded contamination_type within 50 cm.
  • Protic: “showing no soil horizon development, with the exception of a cryic horizon”. It only checked for five subsurface horizons (cambic, argic, spodic, ferralic, nitic), so the example Arenosol (sideralic properties) was named Protic, and the function also passed on a Leptosol with an umbric horizon and the Technosol with a mollic one.
  • Endo- qualifiers built on a diagnostic (Endocalcic, Endogleyic, Endostagnic): “the layer starts >= 50 cm …; and no such layer occurs < 50 cm” (Ch 2.3.1). A horizon starting at 30 cm counted when one of its layers started between 50 and 100 cm. qual_endocalcic() was also defined twice, the copy in force taking any calcic layer between 50 and 200 cm; one definition remains.
